about: Context for translators — not read by the server. `groups`: where the keys under a prefix appear (the longest matching prefix wins). `keys`: a note for one key. `vars`: what each {placeholder} holds; `key_vars` overrides it for one key. scripts/lib/i18n-catalogue.mjs merges this into filex-catalogue-context.json, and web/tests/i18n/langPackCatalogue.test.ts fails when a server key has no group or a placeholder no description.

Email filex sends. Plain text: one line per key, no markup. Written in the RECIPIENT's language as each flow decides it (below).
groups.server.mail.greeting: Email: the first line of every mail filex writes to a person.
groups.server.mail.valid_days: Email (share link, file request): how long the link works.
groups.server.mail.no_expiry: Email (share link, file request): the link has no end date.
Email (share link, file request): a fact line under the introduction — the item, its size, the PIN.
Email: a download link somebody sent from the Share dialog ("Send by email"), or the link an invite falls back to for an address with no account. In the SENDER's language (the one their screen is in).
Email: a file-request (upload) link somebody sent from the Share dialog — the recipient is asked to upload files. In the sender's language.
Email: an existing account was given access to a file or folder (Permissions panel → Invite). In the recipient's account language.
Email: an administrator created an account for the recipient while inviting them; it carries a temporary password. In the language the inviting administrator's screen is in (the new account starts in it too).
Email AND notification to the owner of a folder when somebody uploads files through its file-request link. In the folder owner's account language. The subject is also the notification's stored title.
Email: the administrator's "Send test" in the mail settings. In that administrator's language.
Email (filex cloud sign-up only): the verification token for a new tenant. In the visitor's browser language.
groups.server.mail.app_footer: Email: the line filex adds under every mail an installed app sends (a signature request, a reminder…). In the language the app wrote the mail in.
The first line of NOT.txt, the note filex writes beside files uploaded through a file-request link (the uploader's own note follows). Read by the folder's owner, in their language.
Plugins → Apps → install review and the app's page: what one permission lets the app do. The administrator reads this before trusting the app with their files. Starts with a verb, no final full stop.
The pages a share or file-request link opens in a browser without JavaScript (and a few in any browser: the error pages, the PIN gate, the "preparing your download" page). In the visitor's browser language. Plain text — the page escapes it.
groups.server.public.pin_: Public page: the PIN gate in front of a protected share or file-request link.
groups.server.public.app_: Public page: an app's link (e.g. a signature request) opened without JavaScript — it lists the files the app shared.
groups.server.public.unlocked_: Public page: shown for a moment after a correct PIN, while the download starts.
groups.server.public.zip_: Public page: a shared folder is being packed into a ZIP. zip_hint is the whole sentence and {link} is where the link goes — put it where your language puts it; zip_link is the words inside that link.
groups.server.public.cache_: Public page: a big file on slow storage is copied locally before the download starts.
groups.server.public.folder_: Public page: a shared folder's file list.
groups.server.public.file_count: Public page: a shared folder's file list — the counts line "3 folders · 12 files".
groups.server.public.err_: Public page: a share link that cannot be served (title + one sentence).
groups.server.public.err_drop_: Public page: a file-request link that cannot be used (title + one sentence).
groups.server.public.drop_: Public page: the file-request (upload) page — a stranger uploads files into somebody's folder and cannot see its contents.
groups.server.public.drop_err_: Public page (file request): an upload the page refuses, or the server refused.
groups.server.public.drop_limit_: Public page (file request): the limits line under the drop zone, parts joined with " · ".
groups.server.public.footer: Public pages: the line at the bottom of every page. {filex} becomes the link to filex.sh — keep it exactly once.
groups.server.public.signing_in: The one-second page between single sign-on and the admin panel.
groups.server.public.continue: The one-second page between single sign-on and the admin panel: the link shown when the browser does not move on by itself.
A notification — the bell, the browser's pop-up and the desktop app's — about one event. Composed by the READER's screen in their language from what happened. Title: what happened, to what. Body: where, or the detail. Placeholders the event does not carry are removed together with the dash, arrow or colon next to them.
A word a notification OR an email uses when the event does not say it (an upload with no name typed, a file with no name). One word, both surfaces — they were written twice until v0.43.0.
Admin panel (Users → Add / Edit) and the profile form: why an email address or a username was refused. Shown under the field it is about, in the reader's language. One sentence with a final full stop.
Admin panel (API / MCP) and a person's own API tokens: why the list of scopes (permissions) for a new token was refused. The scope names themselves (read, write, delete, mcp, admin, root:…) are typed by the person and stay in English.
Admin panel → Identity providers: why a change to a sign-in provider was refused, or the question asked before switching on a provider whose test failed.
groups.server.auth_provider.from_: Admin panel → Identity providers: where the environment defines a sign-in provider; used as {from} in server.auth_provider.environment_managed.
Admin panel → Apps → an installed app's schedule: what the app's hourly wake-up amounted to, shown after the app's own summary, e.g. "nothing to do — 0 scheduled, 2 refused (…)". The parts are joined by server.list.separator.
groups.server.list.separator: Between the items of a short list the server writes (e.g. an app's wake-up tally). A comma and a space in most languages; Arabic writes "، ".
Admin panel → Updates: why the newest release will (or will not) be installed by itself, shown under the version number. In the reader's language.
Admin panel → Updates: the name of an update policy (FILEX_UPDATE_POLICY), used as {policy} in server.update.reason.* sentences. Short, lower case.
Admin panel → External services (ONLYOFFICE, draw.io, the converter): why a service's settings were refused.
Admin panel → Storages (Add storage / edit a storage): why the storage's settings were refused. Shown as the error when saving. File and folder patterns (.git, *.tmp, downloads/incomplete/**) and the example folder names stay as written.
A unit after a size — in emails (the size of a shared file) and on the no-JavaScript folder page: "1,5 MB". The same units the interface writes (the unit.* keys); a language that writes "Mo" or "Go" there writes them here too.

keys.server.update.policy.manual: The stored value of the update policy setting (FILEX_UPDATE_POLICY=manual) said the way a person reads it — filex announces a release and installs nothing. Translate the MEANING ("announce only"), not the key’s word "manual".
keys.server.notify.word.someone: Used where a person would be named and nobody is: the {who} of an upload whose visitor typed no name — in the bell AND in the owner’s email.
keys.server.notify.word.unnamed: Used where a file would be named and it has none: the {name} of a notification, and the {name} in a share email’s subject and fact line.
keys.server.mail.drop_invite.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.grant.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.account.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.drop_received.subject: Subject line, and the notification's stored title.
keys.server.mail.smtp_test.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.cloud_verify.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.cloud_verify.how: {ttl} is written by the server as a duration such as 24h0m0s.
keys.server.public.folder_title_suffix: After the folder's name in the browser tab: "Photos — shared folder".
keys.server.public.pin_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the PIN box.
keys.server.public.drop_zone_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the drop zone.
keys.server.public.drop_remove_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the ✕ beside a picked file.
keys.server.public.drop_name_ph: Example text inside the empty name box — use a typical name of the language.
keys.server.notify.plugin.notice.body: An installed app's own notification: "<app name>: <the app's message>".

vars.name: a file or folder name, as it is on disk
vars.link: a clickable link, already made — put it where your language puts it; the words inside it are their own key
vars.site: the site name the administrator set (Settings → Branding)
vars.size: a size with its unit, e.g. 1.4 MB
vars.types: file extensions, comma-separated, e.g. pdf, jpg
vars.who: the uploader's name as they typed it, or the word for "someone"
vars.submission: the name of the new sub-folder the upload was put in, e.g. 2026-09-22_101500_Ana
vars.item: the storage and path of the item, e.g. Files://Reports/2026
vars.url: the address of the sign-in page
vars.email: the email address of the new account
vars.ttl: how long the token lasts, e.g. 24h0m0s
vars.app: the installed app's name, e.g. Signatures
vars.host: an internet host name, e.g. api.example.com
vars.engine: a conversion program's name, e.g. ffmpeg
vars.filex: the word filex as a link to filex.sh — keep it exactly once
vars.path: the file's path inside its storage, e.g. /Reports/2026/q3.pdf
vars.reason: the storage's own error message, in English
vars.signature: the virus scanner's name for what it found
vars.from: the path the item was at
vars.to: the path the item is at now
vars.uploader: the uploader's name as they typed it, or the word for "someone"
vars.body: the first 200 characters of the comment
vars.notice_title: the installed app's own title for its notification
vars.notice_body: the installed app's own text for its notification
vars.op: the replica operation that failed (write, delete, move)
vars.scope: a scope (permission) name exactly as the person typed it
vars.char: the one character that is not allowed, e.g. ş
vars.policy: the update policy's name, one of the server.update.policy.* words

server.public.drop_remove_aria.name: the name of a file the visitor picked

server.public.drop_err_too_large.name: the name of a file the visitor picked

server.public.drop_err_ext.name: the name of a file the visitor picked

server.drop.note_from.name: the uploader's name as they typed it

server.mail.drop_invite.subject.folder: the name of the folder files are requested into

server.mail.drop_invite.limit.count: the most files one upload may carry

server.public.drop_limit_files.count: the most files one upload may carry

server.public.drop_err_too_many.count: the most files one upload may carry

server.account.email_invalid.email: the address as the person typed it

server.account.username_short.count: the fewest characters a username may have

server.account.username_long.count: the most characters a username may have

server.auth_provider.environment_managed.name: the sign-in provider's name, e.g. oidc
server.auth_provider.environment_managed.from: where the environment defines it (a server.auth_provider.from_* sentence, or the variable name FILEX_AUTH_DRIVERS)

server.auth_provider.last_sign_in_method.name: the sign-in provider's name, e.g. oidc

server.auth_provider.from_file.path: the config file's path on the server

server.app.wake.scheduled.count: how many tasks the app asked for in this hour

server.app.wake.beyond.count: how many tasks fall after this hour (they are asked for again later)

server.app.wake.refused.reason: the first refusal's reason, as the server's validation wrote it (English)

server.update.reason.below_minimum.version: the oldest filex version this release can be upgraded from, e.g. 0.40.0

server.storage.scan_exclude_syntax.pattern: the pattern (one line of the setting) as the administrator typed it

server.storage.scan_exclude_everything.pattern: the pattern (one line of the setting) as the administrator typed it

server.storage.scan_exclude_limit.max: the most patterns one storage may have (200)
server.storage.scan_exclude_limit.length: the most characters one pattern may have (512)
